name: Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals

exam.notes: Earns Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals (replaces AI-900, which third-party sources report retired June 30, 2026). Beta announced April 15, 2026; now generally available (exam page shows no beta notice, retirement date: none). Duration not stated on the official pages; 45 minutes is the typical Fundamentals length and is unverified. Delivered via Pearson VUE and Certiport. Hands-on focus on Microsoft Foundry and Python SDK.

objectives.name: Describe principles of responsible AI
bullets: Describe considerations for fairness in an AI solution
Describe considerations for reliability and safety in an AI solution
Describe considerations for privacy and security in an AI solution
Describe considerations for inclusiveness in an AI solution
Describe considerations for transparency in an AI solution
Describe considerations for accountability in an AI solution

objectives.name: Identify AI model components and configurations
bullets: Describe how generative AI models work
Identify an appropriate AI model, based on capabilities
Identify appropriate model deployment options and configuration parameters

objectives.name: Identify AI workloads
bullets: Identify scenarios for common AI workloads, including generative and agentic AI, text analysis, speech, computer vision, and information extraction
Describe common text analysis techniques, including keyword extraction, entity detection, sentiment analysis, and summarization
Identify features and capabilities of speech recognition and speech synthesis
Identify features and capabilities of computer vision and image-generation models
Identify techniques to extract information from text, images, audio, and videos

domains.name: Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry

objectives.name: Implement generative AI apps and agents by using Foundry
bullets: Create effective system and user prompts for generative AI models
Deploy a model and interact with it in the Foundry portal
Create a lightweight chat client application by using the Foundry SDK
Create and test a single-agent solution in the Foundry portal
Create a lightweight client application for an agent

objectives.name: Implement AI solutions for text and speech by using Foundry
bullets: Build a lightweight application that includes text analysis
Respond to spoken prompts by using a deployed multimodal model
Build a lightweight application by using Azure Speech in Foundry Tools

objectives.name: Implement AI solutions with computer vision and image-generation capabilities by using Foundry
bullets: Interpret visual input in prompts by using a deployed multimodal model
Create new visual outputs by using generative models
Build a lightweight application that includes vision capabilities

objectives.name: Implement AI solutions for information extraction by using Foundry
bullets: Extract information from documents and forms by using Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools
Extract information from images by using Content Understanding
Extract information from audio and video by using Content Understanding
Build a lightweight application with information extraction capabilities by using Content Understanding

caveats: Outline fetched from the official AI-901 study guide (skills measured as of April 15, 2026). AI-901 replaces AI-900 for the Azure AI Fundamentals certification; AI-900 retirement on June 30, 2026 is reported by third-party sources (official certification page now lists only AI-901). Beta began April 15, 2026 (third-party report), now appears live. Exam duration and question count are not published on the official pages; 45 minutes / 40-60 questions are typical Fundamentals values. Localized outlines lag ~8 weeks. Classic ML (regression/clustering, Azure ML) that featured in AI-900 is not explicitly in the AI-901 outline. 'Foundry Tools' is the current branding for the former Azure AI Services.
